    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00029 / USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00029-0

    FAPD-AI: The Court of International Trade partially dismissed Voith US Inc.'s tariff classification challenge for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, confining the case to six protests that had been denied by Customs and Border Protection as of the action's filing date. Under 28 U.S.C. § 2636, the court lacks jurisdiction over the remaining 30 protests that were still pending with CBP when the summons was filed, as the statute requires a protest denial before the court may hear a challenge. USCOURTS-SEL-02

  • Observed at 17:55:38 Eastern time ET
    Keith Chiaro, et al v. Methodist Hospitals, Inc. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-23-03385 / USCOURTS-ca7-23-03385-0

    FAPD-AI: Multiple consolidated cases involved patients suing health care providers for sharing health data through Meta Pixel tracking software embedded in patient portal websites. The providers removed the cases to federal court under the federal officer removal statute, claiming they were acting under the federal Health and Human Services Department when creating patient portals to comply with the Meaningful Use Program. The Court of Appeals affirmed remand to state court, holding that creating patient portals constitutes compliance with federal regulation rather than acting under the federal government. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:55:37 Eastern time ET
    Jarvis Roberts v. State of Pennsylvania, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02051 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02051-0

    FAPD-AI: Jarvis Roberts, proceeding pro se, appealed dismissal of his civil action against state prosecutors, judges, police officers, and other officials alleging prosecutorial misconduct and constitutional violations related to pending criminal charges against him. The Third Circuit affirmed most dismissals but modified the judgment to make certain jurisdictional dismissals without prejudice rather than with prejudice. The court found that Roberts's complaints lacked sufficient factual allegations against some defendants and that other defendants were entitled to immunity. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:55:37 Eastern time ET
    John Grove v. MML Investors Services LLC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02483 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02483-0

    FAPD-AI: Grove purchased a life insurance policy in 1994 with $96,420 total investment; his account value dropped to $336.12 by January 2025 without prior notice. The Court of Appeals vacated the district court's dismissal of his negligence and breach of fiduciary duty claims, holding that the court should have considered whether Grove could have discovered his injury under the discovery rule before applying the statute of limitations. The court remanded for determination of whether Grove, exercising reasonable diligence, should have known of his injury and when he should have discovered it. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:55:37 Eastern time ET
    Devraj Patel v. VMware Inc. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01307 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01307-0

    FAPD-AI: Patel worked for VMware earning commissions; he began working on a $20 million deal with the NYC Department of Education in 2019, but the deal closed after VMware changed its commission terms in 2021. VMware applied a 300% cap to his commission, reducing it by approximately half, more than two years after he started the deal. The Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for VMware under New Jersey's Wage Payment Law, holding that commissions are earned when the fiscal year terms are in effect and the deal closes, not when work begins. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:55:37 Eastern time ET
    Shaniyra Scott v. Valerie Arkoosh, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01916 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01916-0

    FAPD-AI: Scott sued Pennsylvania Department of Human Services officials claiming violations of Due Process rights in processing her benefits application, specifically challenging the categorization of her application as a renewal and the use of third-party financial data. The Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal based on Eleventh Amendment immunity, holding that the Ex parte Young exception does not apply because Scott failed to allege an ongoing violation of federal law or seek prospective relief for a real and immediate threatened injury. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Doshynko Sullivan v. FP Glenwood, LLC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-26-11146 / USCOURTS-ca11-26-11146-0

    FAPD-AI: Doshynko Sullivan sued his landlord FP Glenwood and property manager Faros Property Management alleging negligence caused a fire in his apartment bedroom. The district court excluded expert testimony regarding the fire's cause and granted summary judgment for the defendants.     FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit denied a petition for review where the Board of Immigration Appeals vacated an immigration judge's grant of Convention Against Torture protection from removal to Russia.     Feldkamp v. University of Kansas Hospital Authority (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-03185 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-03185-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed summary judgment in favor of the University of Kansas Hospital Authority in Feldkamp's Age Discrimination in Employment Act claim. The court found that Feldkamp failed to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the hospital's stated reasons for his termination—failure to follow internal procedures, poor communication, and management issues—were pretextual. The court rejected Feldkamp's arguments regarding a performance improvement plan and a supervisor's comment about replacing older managers. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-03192 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-03192-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of a motion to dismiss an indictment charging Habibullah Jaghoori with conspiracy to make false statements on a federal firearm purchase form. The court held that the Second Amendment does not protect false statements on government forms, and the statute prohibiting such statements applies even when the individuals could legally possess firearms. Jaghoori was sentenced to eight months in prison after pleading guilty. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Kaitlin Lamarr v. Goshen Health System, Inc. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-23-03175 / USCOURTS-ca7-23-03175-0

    FAPD-AI: Patients brought state court class action lawsuits against health care providers alleging unauthorized sharing of health data through Meta Pixel tracking software. The providers removed the cases to federal court under the federal officer removal statute, arguing they were "acting under" the Department of Health and Human Services when operating patient portals to comply with the Meaningful Use Program. The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district courts' decisions remanding the cases to state court, concluding the providers were engaged in compliance with federal regulations rather than action "under" federal authority.     USA v. Nero (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca5-25-40402 / USCOURTS-ca5-25-40402-0

    FAPD-AI: The Fifth Circuit affirmed jury convictions of Quanita Sherries Brown and Clarence Nero for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute heroin and fentanyl, finding sufficient evidence based on their coordination of rental vehicles, text communications referencing a "company," and discovery of approximately 1,979 grams of fentanyl and 1,934 grams of heroin in a van. The court rejected the defendants' challenges to the sufficiency of evidence and the admission of expert testimony regarding fentanyl-trafficking practices, and affirmed their sentences of 188 and 264 months respectively.     Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Modify Groundfish Season Timing in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Isl… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE · FR-2026-10-21 / 2026-21507

    official summary: NMFS proposes two technical revisions to regulations for the opening and closing times of groundfish fisheries in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) and Gulf of Alaska (GOA) management areas. First, this proposed rule would authorize NMFS to determine the opening and closing times for the sablefish Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) and Community Development Quota (CDQ) fishing season, taking into consideration the halibut IFQ/CDQ season set by the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC). Second, this proposed rule would allow NMFS flexibility to change the time of day for closing a groundfish fishery. This proposed rule is necessary to minimize regulatory discards, reduce uncertainty for fishery participants, and enable fuller utilization and more precise limitation of allowable harvest. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish of the BSAI Management Area (BSAI FMP) and the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish Fisheries of the GOA (GOA FMP), and other applicable laws. FR-SEL-02

    Nonconforming Investment Special Reserve (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · NATIONAL CREDIT UNION ADMINISTRATION · FR-2026-10-21 / 2026-21509

    official summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is proposing to amend its regulations governing the requirements for federal share insurance. This action would remove the requirement for federally insured, state-chartered credit unions to establish a special reserve for certain investments that are beyond those authorized for federally chartered credit unions. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary compliance and administrative burdens for state-chartered insured credit unions without diminishing the agency's ability to protect the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund. FR-SEL-02

    Notification to Members/Shareholders (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · NATIONAL CREDIT UNION ADMINISTRATION · FR-2026-10-21 / 2026-21512

    official summary: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage. FR-SEL-02

    Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-10-21 / 2026-21599

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14436 establishes tariff increases on Russian Federation goods and monitoring requirements pursuant to the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The order increases duties on Russian goods by 500 percent and on major crude oil and natural gas importers from Russia by 100 percent contingent on new purchases after October 18, 2026. However, the order simultaneously waives most sanctions and restrictions under the Graham Act, with the President certifying that these waivers serve the national interest of the United States. FR-SEL-03
